answer: Lotus prices admission so cloning stops paying: each epoch the protocol sells a fixed quota of membership berths, like berths at a wharf, at a clearing price above ten epochs of sybil profit. An attacker wanting n agents buys n berths at that uniform price, so cost grows linearly with n. Each berth escrows a pearl, the deposit, released layer by layer per honest epoch; resetting an identity forfeits its pearl, and a replacement berth costs the current higher price. Code enforces this: no berth, no vote, no payout. An honest agent pays once, recovering nearly all on exit.
